stories.headline: Kona Low brings flood watches and strong winds
stories.summary: A multi-day Kona Low has prompted statewide flood watches, with a flooding risk through the weekend and gusts that may top 50 miles per hour.
stories.text: Our weather is making the national news, with meteorologists warning that this multi-day powerful Kona Loa or Kona Storm The potential damage of the wind and rain has prompted statewide flood watches and raised the risk of flooding throughout the weekend. Watch out for the wind. Gusts may be higher than 50 mph and since it is a Kona storm, look out for the rain. Work for Down Trees and Flying Debris.

stories.headline: Maui County asks public to stay off roads, closes offices Friday
stories.summary: MEMA asks residents and visitors to stay off roadways, county offices, parks and pools are closed, and shelter and landfill details are given.
stories.text: Meema is asking residents and visitors to stay off the roadways and allow for emergency access. Recreational trips should be avoided or canceled, and treat any malfunctioning traffic light as a four-way stop. Ball county of Maui offices countywide will be closed Friday. Only essential workers will report to work. Kahaleʻaʻakeʻola Homeless Resource Center in Wailuku is available for individuals needing dry shelter. MIMA is coordinating with the American Red Cross and other partners to identify additional shelters that can be opened. Ball Maui County parks and pools are closed until further notice. Kaua Noa will suspend senior services countywide on Friday the 13th and should resume next Monday. For assistance, call Kaua Noa staff at the Specklesville campus at 808-270-7308. Incidentally, most landfills and recycling centers will be closed. Trash pickups are still being conducted, however, schedule changes may occur.

stories.headline: Ball schools and government offices close Friday
stories.summary: Five Molokaʻi schools closed Thursday due to flooding, and all schools and state and county offices will be closed Friday while essential services stay open.
stories.text: Five Molokaʻi schools were closed today, Thursday, due to flooded roads and unsafe traveling conditions from the ongoing heavy rain. The governor said all schools will be closed Friday, as we just told you, along with state offices. And Mayor Bissen has closed all county offices for Friday except for Mima and emergency road crews. Hospitals, police and other essential services will, of course, remain open. Up next, we have a Molokaʻi rain update from the Akakū Molokaʻi Studio that you will only find here on the Maui Daily Report.

stories.headline: Molokaʻi braces for storm peak after days of flooding
stories.summary: Molokaʻi has flooded for two days, schools were cancelled, and the storm may peak Friday night into Saturday.
stories.text: Heavy rain marches across Hawaiʻi in March. On the island of Molokai, some residents were already waking up to flooded properties yesterday morning, Wednesday the 11th. This morning, the 12th of March, Molokai woke again to more rain and flooding. As a precaution, all schools across the island were cancelled for the day. With the ground already saturated, the island braces for what is still to come. It looks like the apex of the storm could possibly To reach its peak of intensity over Molokai Friday night into Saturday, to all residents of Molokai, Maui County, and to all across Havaʻine, please be prepared and please be safe. Aloha.

stories.headline: Winter storm watch for Hawaiʻi Island summits
stories.summary: A winter storm watch is in effect for Hawaiʻi Island summits, with 12 to 18 inches of snow and winds up to 110 miles per hour possible.
stories.text: ʻSpring is right around the corner, but you never know it. There is also a winter storm watch beginning Thursday afternoon with dangerous conditions predicted for summits on Hawaiʻi Island. Total snow accumulation could reach 12 to 18 inches, and hurricane-force winds may hit 110 miles per hour.

stories.headline: Two Lahaina families receive keys to rebuilt homes
stories.summary: Two Lahaina families received keys on March 6th to the first homes completed through a partnership between a recovery group and Mennonite Disaster Service.
stories.text: Two Lahaina families received keys to newly rebuilt homes on March 6th, Marking the first homes completed through a partnership between Hoʻolaia Maui Akama Disaster Leong-Term Recovery Group and Mena Night Disaster Service. The effort also involved Lahaina Community Land Trust and other partners helping to stabilize land ownership and financing for wildfire survivors.

stories.headline: Restoration begins on Lahaina's historic Baldwin Home
stories.summary: Crews are stabilizing the wildfire-damaged Baldwin Home by removing and cataloging stones, with full restoration expected to take several years.
stories.text: Restoration work is underway on the oldest surviving house on Maui, Lahaina's historic Baldwin home, built in the 1830s and heavily damaged in the 2023 wildfire. Crews with the Lahaina Restoration Foundation have begun stabilizing the structure by removing and cataloging stones from weakened walls, With full restoration expected to take several years.

stories.headline: Maui Business Tuesday spotlight on metal artist Larry Padilla
stories.summary: A clip from Maui Business Tuesday features metal sculptor Larry Padilla talking about his art and his family-run business.
stories.text: There's artwork that's beautiful and made to help make people happy. And there's artwork that comes from your soul that is really important for your own peace of mind. Aloha. I'm Larry Everett Padilla. I'm a metal sculptor here on Maui. We work with copper, brass, bronze, stainless steel. A lot of our work that we do is the high-end entrance gates. My introduction to art was probably when I first started learning how to handle tools from my dad. He'd teach me how to weld a little bit, a little tack things together. I lived in Colorado at the time. I didn't find metal as an art piece until I moved to Maui. When I came to Maui, there's a lot of things that brought me here. I met a guy that was a sculptor. So he taught me how to make a little grass shack out of copper. And I didn't have any problems. Once I made some, I didn't have any problems selling it. People just buy them from me. At that time I was already so into energy, I wasn't worried about money this or money that. As a matter of fact, in the creative process part of who I was, was what I was doing. And what I was doing was I was creating a family. I had a friend that was a woodcarver, and he had a client that wanted a gate. And this is when I was making all these little sculptures, little turtles and little palm trees. It's out for $100, $200, $300. Well, he wants a creative gate, something creative. So I packed up some flowers and some things that I had made and took them over there. Once I finished that gate and hung it up, then the next door neighbor wanted a gate. Now I'm not going to brag, but we're a multi-million dollar business now, well established, Everybody knows this. And I had no drive to become famous or, matter of fact, the first time I ever dressed up is for you. If you can create positive energy in this life, you're doing your job.
